sources.entry: OrcaReplay by Continuum AI - Records a Claude Code run through a local proxy and replays it offline, reproducing it byte-for-byte with the network off, or forking it from any checkpoint onto a different model. Capture happens below the harness, so shell exit codes, per-turn file changes and MCP calls land on the same timeline as the model traffic. (NB: Status: "Early")
OrcaReplay - Records a coding-agent run and replays it back to the agent with no model called, or forks a checkpoint onto other models to compare. #free

summary.one_liner: OrcaReplay is a local proxy-based recorder for coding-agent runs that can replay a recording offline with no model called, or fork it from a checkpoint onto a different model for comparison.
summary.what_it_does: Records a coding agent's run by standing up a local proxy and setting base-URL environment variables, capturing model requests and streamed responses, plus shell exit codes and timings, per-turn filesystem changes, and MCP traffic on one timeline. Replay mode serves the recorded run from disk with network egress blocked, so no model is called and no tokens are spent; the README says recorded tool calls still execute for real. A cursor can be placed at a checkpoint so that later turns are answered by a different model, and a compare command runs several models from the same checkpoint and grades each with a user-supplied command. Output includes a per-run HTML timeline, an event/graph view, SVG/PNG/GIF export of failure chains, and JSON output for scripts. It also supports pushing and pulling runs to a gateway, and serves the trace store over MCP. The README is closely tied to its authors' OrcaRouter gateway, which is the default gateway for the setup command.
use_cases: debug why a coding agent broke something
replay an agent run offline without spending tokens
compare coding models on the same task from a checkpoint
record Claude Code or Codex CLI sessions for later review
share an agent run as an HTML or SVG artifact in an issue
feed run traces to an agent over MCP
notable: Capture happens below the agent at the proxy/socket boundary, so the agent does not need modification
Replay with egress blocked reproduces recorded model traffic byte-for-byte without calling a model
Fork from any derived checkpoint onto a different model, with the model as the only variable
Per-run HTML timeline that works offline as a single file with no external references
Optional TLS interception with a per-run CA to capture harnesses that cannot be redirected, such as Codex CLI with ChatGPT login
caveats: Replay is not a sandbox: recorded tool calls execute for real, and shell or MCP commands that open their own sockets are outside the no-egress guarantee
Several agent integrations are documented as having caveats, such as goose shell calls lacking real exit codes unless recorded with --no-shell
The listing marks the project status as Early, and the README is heavily tied to the OrcaRouter gateway (the default gateway, and the push/pull feature needs a gateway key)
keywords: run an agent again without tokens
test different model on coding task
